adamrk opened PR #15042 from adamrk:abk/hyper-error-to-guest to bytecodealliance:main:

Ensure that an error encountered when sending a request or response body is delivered to the associated transmit future when the body is coming from another host body which has been forwarded.

Previously a guest which forwards a request or response would have no way to see if the request/response body was delivered without error. For example, if the original sender passed a body with incorrect content length or if it dropped the connection before completion, the guest would still receive Ok(()) on the transmission future.

cfallin commented on PR #15042:

Tagging in @pchickey to review; I'm not familiar enough with the code here to sign off (though it looks plausible to me).

xia-chao commented on PR #15042:

not sure if this is related to #15111, but dropping a forwarded body early still
gives the guest Ok from transmit. expected?

adamrk commented on PR #15042:

I don't really think this is quite the same as the issues in https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/issues/15111. Here we're just ensuring that when the request produces an error, a guest which forwarded that request sees it.

:memo: rvolosatovs submitted PR review:

sorry for the delay on the review.

Could we keep the BodyWithContentLength wrapper and instead add the error report wrapper next to it?

We'd need to move the error_tx out of BodyWithContentLength.

adamrk commented on PR #15042:

Could we keep the BodyWithContentLength wrapper and instead add the error report wrapper next to it?

Yep, changed it to have a separate body type for the error which we wrap around BodyWithContentLength.
